correctness.rationale: Necessity follows from Aubry--Iezzi Proposition 5.2 and the delta=1 genus difference; uniqueness of the F25-maximal elliptic curve follows from characteristic-five Hasse invariant and six j=0 twists. F25-Frobenius [-5] gives E(F625)=E[24], the surjective [-6] difference with kernel E[6], and complete orbit comparison under E[6] rtimes mu6. The action on E[4] has orbit sizes 3,6,6; lifting branches yields 54,108,108 and stabilizers of sizes 4,2,2; the first is V4 via two commuting involutions. The pure-Python verifier recomputed the finite orbits and 270 closed points from scratch. No numerical experiment is used as a substitute for the universal geometric arguments.

value.rationale: The recent construction singles out a geometrically natural minimal positive-genus singular-maximal setting. Classifying all its k-isomorphism classes, rather than just producing one curve or counting the degree-two gluing points, identifies a nontrivial moduli quotient. The exact F25 elliptic four-torsion orbit partition and full singular-curve automorphism groups distinguish the global arithmetic geometry of three classes despite identical zeta functions and singularity type; the two nontrivial primitive orbits are not separated by group order. This is a complete classification with a motivated point and automorphism invariant, not an arbitrary slice or a routine substitution.
